page.title: Harness skill

frontmatter.name: harness
frontmatter.description: Work harness items from your own Claude Code or Codex session through the platform's MCP surface, from sign-in to submitting a pull request at the gate.

page.bodyMd:
You work items on the unfoldingWord harness from your own machine. Everything you do on the platform goes through its MCP surface; you never call any other part of it. Follow these steps in order.

## Sign in

Sign in to Cloudflare Access with your own Google account:

```
cloudflared access login https://<uw-app>/mcp
```

Add the platform as an MCP server named `uw-platform` at `https://<uw-app>/mcp`, sending your Access token and an `x-uw-device` header that names this machine (for example `x-uw-device: laptop`). The platform mints you as `agent:<you>/<device>`. A scheduled routine that runs without you uses a service token instead and must name a live delegation when it claims.

## Poll

Call `poll_queue` with `harnessId` (or `null` for every harness you may work) and a `limit`. It lists only the items you may claim, highest priority first.

## Claim

Call `claim_item` with the item's `itemId`. Pass `delegationId` when a scheduled routine claims under a delegation, and `null` when you claim for yourself. The reply carries your lease, its expiry and the branch to work on: `harness/<item>`, a commit to start from, and whether you adopted an existing branch.

## Worktree

Make a git worktree for the item on its branch, starting from the commit the claim named:

```
git worktree add ../<item> -b harness/<item> <expected head>
```

If the claim adopted an existing branch, check out `harness/<item>` in the worktree instead.

## Context

Call `resolve_context` with the `itemId`. It answers the item's instructions page, its package pages and the learnings that apply. Read them before you change anything.

## Work and record

Work in the worktree. After every step (`read`, `scout`, `work`, `submit`), call `record_run_step` with the `itemId`, a `runId` you choose for this item (a UUID, the same one for every step of the item), the `step`, `tokensIn` and `tokensOut` from your session, and `costBasis: subscription`. Send no cost: your subscription is not counted against the platform's spend. Read `prompts` in every reply; a person may have sent you a message.

## The lease warning

When a reply carries `leaseWarning: true`, your lease is about to expire. Commit everything in the worktree as `wip: <item>` and push it to `harness/<item>` with your own git credentials, so the work survives if the lease lapses. The platform holds no checkpoint of your work.

## Pull request

Open a pull request from `harness/<item>` into the default branch. Its body opens with the fenced `harness` declaration, before anything else:

```harness
closes: #<issue>
risks: <what could break, in one line>
touches: <the areas you changed, comma-separated>
risk_tier: <low, medium or high>
risk_domains: <the risk domains, comma-separated, or none>
```

## Submit

Call `submit_to_gate` with the `itemId`, your `evidence`, `to: null`, the `pullRequest` (`repo` and `number`) and the `head` commit you pushed. The item moves on, or parks for a person to decide.

## What you never do

You never approve, merge, deploy or publish, and you never advance an item past a human gate. No verb exists for any of them; a person decides at the gate.
